Subject: Moving accelerator credits when we convert to Dedicated?

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick follow-up from our cohort team: we have $12k in accelerator credits held in escrow for the BlueSprout founders account, and we're planning to convert one of our portfolio startups to a Redwood Dedicated seat next month. The founders asked whether those escrowed accelerators can be applied to the Dedicated subscription (either transferred or used as a balance against first-month invoices) when they convert.

Two constraints on our side:
- We need billing to reflect the transfer on day one of the Dedicated subscription (startup can’t wait for a refund cycle)
- Finance will require a simple reconciliation PDF and a W9 submitted before we can accept any invoice adjustments

Is this something Redwood can support? If yes, what information do you need (account IDs, company legal name, any contract addenda)? If there are thresholds or approvals required, please let me know so I can loop internal stakeholders.

Hi Liz —

Great question and congrats to the founders on the upcoming conversion. Short answer: we can support a couple of paths depending on the timing and accounting preferences. I outlined two options and the info we need below.

Option A — Escrow transfer + day-one crediting (preferred)
- We mark the $12k as an escrow transfer on our side and apply it as a credit to the Dedicated subscription invoice on day one.
- Requires: account ID for the Dedicated seat, legal entity name, and the W9 you attached.
- Limit: we can only apply promo/escrow credits to consumption-related charges (tokens/embeddings) and not to third-party infra fees.

Option B — One-time invoice adjustment (if legal/procurement prefers)
- We invoice at full price and issue a one-time credit memo post-activation.
- This is slower (refund/credit cycles) but cleaner for audit trails.

Approval & thresholds
- Any escrow transfer above $5k needs Sales Ops approval and a short written exception. I can fast-track that internally once you confirm the account ID and sign-off from your finance contact.

Next steps I propose:
1) Send me the Dedicated account ID and the exact legal name to show on the credit memo.
2) Confirm you’re comfortable with Option A (day-one crediting) or pick Option B.
3) Share the finance contact who will accept the W9 and final reconciliation PDF.

I attached a short one-pager that explains how escrow transfers map to invoices and timing so your ops folks can review. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if it helps.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Startups & Programs
Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0124
